subject: Multi-region volume trigger and reseller-margin gating for private offer
messages:
From: Sarah Li <sarah.li@acmehealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Wed, 28 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Multi-region volume triggers & reseller margin gating (cloud marketplace private offer)

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the walkthrough last week. We’re getting the procurement team aligned on the private offer for Acme Health but have two cross-region pricing mechanics we need clarified before legal will sign off:

1) Volume triggers: Acme operates in US + EU regions. We need to confirm whether volume triggers will be evaluated per-region (AWS/GCP separately) or aggregated globally for the private offer. Our infra is split, but we prefer a single global commitment for predictability.

2) Reseller margin gating: our reseller partners expect a margin floor for their downstream carriage. We can accept a pass-through mechanism, but procurement wants a gating clause that prevents reseller uplift above an agreed % if monthly usage falls below a threshold (to avoid payback disputes). In plain terms: if monthly usage < X% of committed run-rate, the reseller margin/carve should be capped or provide a rebate path.

I've attached an expected consumption workbook (ACME_Expected_Consumption.xlsx) that sketches month-by-month. Can you share recommended language and how redwood handles invoicing routing and global aggregation? We’d also like a short example with numbers (committed units, trigger %, reseller carve).

Can we target a call early next week (Mon/Tue) to finalize?

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Li
Director, Cloud Procurement
Acme Health

From: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Li <sarah.li@acmehealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Mar 2028 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Multi-region volume triggers & reseller margin gating (cloud marketplace private offer)

Thanks Sarah — appreciate the attachment, this is helpful. High level answers and an option set below; happy to walk through on Monday.

Option A — Global aggregation (recommended)
- Commit and triggers are evaluated across regions (US + EU aggregate).
- Reseller margin gating is applied to the aggregated usage to avoid per-region cliff effects.
- Invoicing: marketplace passes revenue to Redwood per-region; Redwood aggregates for rebate/true-up calculations.

Option B — Per-region triggers
- Triggers evaluated per-cloud region/SKU. More precision, higher complexity.

Example (global aggregation):
- Committed: 1,200 reserved units/month across all regions (annualized 14,400).
- Trigger threshold: 75% of committed (900 units/month).
- Reseller carve baseline: 10% of list; gating: if monthly usage < 50% of committed, reseller carve temporarily capped at 5% and a usage-based rebate accrues to Acme for months below threshold.

Suggested clause language (short):
"If aggregated monthly delivered units are below 50% of the committed monthly run-rate, reseller margin shall be reduced to a capped rate of 5% for the applicable month(s). Any shortfall will accrue a pro-rated rebate credited at the next true-up. Parties will use marketplace metering as the single source of truth."

I attached a draft of Redwood_PO_Terms_Draft.pdf with the gating clause highlighted. For next steps I recommend:
- Confirm whether Acme is comfortable with global aggregation (low friction for ops).
- If yes, we’ll route the draft to Legal + Marketplace Ops for final SKU mapping.

Proposed call windows: Mon Apr 2, 10:00–11:30 PT or Tue Apr 3, 08:00–09:00 PT. Which works?

Best,
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Mar 2028 09:00:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Multi-region volume triggers & reseller margin gating — Ops notes

Karthik / Laura — quick ops notes based on Sarah’s ask and the draft:

On Thu, Mar 28, 2028 at 12:05 PM, karthik_iyer wrote:
> Suggested clause language (short):
> "If aggregated monthly delivered units are below 50% of the committed monthly run-rate, reseller margin shall be reduced to a capped rate of 5% for the applicable month(s). Any shortfall will accrue a pro-rated rebate credited at the next true-up. Parties will use marketplace metering as the single source of truth."

Operational considerations (recommendations):
- Invoice routing: use marketplace settlement data as the canonical metering and for monthly true-up calculations. Ops will need to map marketplace SKU -> Redwood SKU -> Acme billing account.
- Grace/smoothing: allow 30-day smoothing window (month N shortfall can be offset by month N+1 usage up to 20% of committed) to avoid churn from seasonal dips.
- Rebate mechanics: accrue credit as a negative line-item on month-end invoice; communicate accruals each billing cycle.
- Reseller carve calculation: recommend fixed % bands by revenue bucket, not flat percent on list price (simpler to administer). Example: 0–$100k -> 8%, $100–$500k -> 10%, >$500k -> 12%.

Draft redline language (excerpt):
"Reseller Margin Gating: In the event that aggregated monthly usage falls below the Lower Threshold (50% of Monthly Commitment), the Reseller Margin for the affected month shall be capped at the Gated Rate (5%). A shortfall credit equal to the pro-rated difference between the baseline Reseller Margin and the Gated Rate shall accrue and be applied at the next billing true-up. Operators shall evaluate usage on a 30-day smoothing window to allow temporal variance."

Questions for Legal:
1) Does the accrual approach create revenue recognition friction? (We should flag to Finance).
2) Any marketplace constraints on negative-line invoice items? (Laura, can Ops confirm with Marketplace Support).

I’ll draft the ops appendix for the draft PO once Laura confirms the invoicing path.

—Ben
Principal, Marketplace Partnerships | Redwood Inference

From: Sarah Li <sarah.li@acmehealth.com>

Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Fri, 31 Mar 2028 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Multi-region volume triggers & reseller margin gating (cloud marketplace private offer)

Karthik,

Thanks — the global aggregation option looks like the best fit for Acme. A few clarifying asks before we route to our legal:  

- Smoothing: we can accept a 30-day smoothing window but would prefer that any accrued credits be visible on the next two invoices (not wait a single quarter).
- Cap on reseller carve: Acme will agree to an initial baseline carve of 10% with a cap mechanism as you suggested, but we request that the maximum carve under normal conditions does not exceed 12% without written approval.
- EU edge: we have a small EU footprint that may have currency/tax variance. Can the gating/rate logic be expressed as percentages so it’s region-agnostic (i.e., avoid hard-dollar rebates)?

If you can produce a final clause incorporating the smoothing and the two invoicing-visibility items, we’ll circulate to Legal and Procurement and push for signature. Also please send a DocuSign link when ready.

Appreciate the responsiveness — we’re aiming to close this PO before mid-April.

Best,
Sarah
Director, Cloud Procurement
Acme Health

Subject: Re: Multi-region volume triggers & reseller margin gating (cloud marketplace private offer)

Sarah — great, thank you. Confirming next steps and owners so we can get this into legal and signature: 

Action items:
- Ben: finalize Ops appendix with invoice routing, 30-day smoothing wording, and accrual line-item examples. (Ben target: Wed Apr 4)
- Laura: confirm marketplace SKU mapping and whether negative invoice line items are supported in AWS Marketplace & GCP Marketplace (Laura target: Wed Apr 4).
- Grace: generate final PO + redline with clause language and create DocuSign envelope for Acme legal review (Grace target: Thu Apr 5).
- Karthik: coordinate legal review and confirm final carve cap at 12% as requested; prepare client-facing summary.

Final clause summary to include in the PO (client-facing):
"Reseller Margin Gating (summary): Aggregated monthly usage across regions will be evaluated against the committed Monthly Run-Rate. If aggregated usage falls below 50% of the Monthly Run-Rate in any given month, the reseller margin for that month will be capped at 5%. A pro-rated shortfall credit will accrue and appear as a negative line-item on the subsequent invoice(s) (visible for up to two billing cycles). Parties agree that percentages will be used for gating and rebates to account for cross-currency and tax differences. The baseline reseller carve for this agreement is 10% with an explicit cap of 12% absent subsequent written consent."

I’ve attached links to the draft terms and the ACME consumption workbook in the Doc (Drive link and DocuSign will be posted). If everyone is aligned, I’ll mark for legal intake first thing tomorrow.

Thanks all — will circle up after Ben/Laura post updates.

Best,
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
